title: WRDO: Weighted Refusal Direction Optimization in Aligned Language Models

claims.claim: WRDO constructs a composite refusal direction from a bank of per-prompt directions using learned aggregation weights.
claims.evidence: We propose Weighted Refusal Direction Optimization (WRDO), a procedure that constructs a composite refusal direction from a bank of per-prompt directions using learned aggregation weights.

claims.claim: WRDO is evaluated against prior single-direction methods on three open-weight language models using three guard judges and HarmBench as an external evaluator.

title: ExGrad: Beyond Suppression - Explicit Clean-Gradient Subtraction in Adversarial Training

claims.claim: ExGrad constructs clean-input, adversarial-input, and adversarial-weight-perturbed gradients to measure margin responses through virtual steps.
claims.evidence: We introduce ExGrad (extrapolative gradient recomposition), which constructs clean-input, adversarial-input, and adversarial-weight-perturbed (AWP) gradients. Virtual steps measure their margin responses,

claims.claim: ExGrad selects coefficients over a bounded affine domain without nonnegativity constraints by solving a globally solvable three-variable problem.
claims.evidence: a globally solvable three-variable problem selects coefficients over a bounded affine domain without nonnegativity constraints.

claims.claim: Negative clean coefficients in ExGrad rapidly predominate and increase in magnitude with the affine radius on CIFAR-10.
claims.evidence: Across affine radii on CIFAR-10, negative clean coefficients rapidly predominate and increase in magnitude with the radius.

claims.claim: Setting the clean coefficient to zero in ExGrad is insufficient, as mild subtraction improves PGD-20 while stronger subtraction trades clean accuracy for further PGD-20 gains.

claims.evidence: Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-100 show radius-dependent improvements over AWP.

title: The role of locality and weight sharing in convolutional neural networks

claims.claim: Convolutional students learn exactly $P$ times faster than locally connected students when positions are uncorrelated.
claims.evidence: For uncorrelated positions ($c = 0$), the two students follow the same learning trajectory, with the convolutional student learning exactly $P$ times faster.

claims.claim: Spatial correlations reduce the advantage of weight sharing in convolutional students.
claims.evidence: For $c > 0$, spatial correlations can reduce the advantage of weight sharing.

claims.claim: The asymptotic error of the convolutional student grows with spatial correlation.
claims.evidence: The asymptotic error of the convolutional student grows with $c$, whereas that of the locally connected student is independent of $c$ and overall lower when evaluated at the same learning rate.

claims.claim: The performance of convolutional and locally connected students depends on the learning rate tuning strategy.
claims.evidence: When the learning rate is instead tuned to the training horizon, however, the locally connected student wins at early times and the convolutional student at late times, with a transition that we predict analytically.
